title: Completion and normalization boundaries
summary: The model proposes completion. native/completion.py verifies the request's required evidence and checks; output/final-response contracts determine what must be delivered. A successful tool.
html:
Completion and normalization boundaries

The model proposes completion. native/completion.py verifies the request's required evidence and checks; output/final-response contracts determine what must be delivered. A successful tool result alone is not permission to stop when other obligations remain.

Completion authority also enforces the user-input control boundary. A required unresolved human interaction blocks successful completion, including Direct Completion. Only model-authored terminal text is inspected for explicit continuation intent; tool output, fenced code and obvious quotations are not interpreted as requests. The reason terminal_continuation_requires_ask_user records rejected completion. The next ordinary decision retains the full tool set allowed by capability and skill policy. The shared internal decision-control envelope supplies the rejection reason, evidence and guidance in every context mode. Advertisement, provider tool choice, single dispatch and batch admission never impose a completion-only restriction. Execution does not count as another completion rejection. Repeated invalid completions use the configured no-progress bound; there is no special two-strike termination. The runtime never manufactures an ASK or an executable action from ambiguous prose.

Completion candidates are advisory. New accepted work invalidates old candidates; steering and evidence revisions also invalidate their acceptance. Deterministic normalization can accept valid metadata and evidence without rewriting the answer. Otherwise the next ordinary task decision chooses what to do, with no dedicated wording-repair model call. Permissions, approvals, lifecycle waits, evidence checks and recorded operation identities keep their existing authority.

The guard runs before terminal presentation is applied. Direct Completion markers carry status/evidence, not final prose; their requested-answer stage uses the same guard. Optional retrospective summaries also reject continuation wording before publication, preserving the already-accepted terminal outcome without another call. Question marks, rhetorical headings and optional suggestions for future requests do not by themselves imply waiting. The lexical fallback is deliberately conservative and is not a general natural-language intent classifier.

Direct completion carries model-declared terminal intent alongside an action, using the retained __smto_completion compatibility field. The runtime removes that metadata from business arguments while preserving the assistant journal. It validates completion only after durable capability results exist. Accumulated evidence can refer to prior receipts; it does not erase unfinished work or requested chat output.

Both answered and completed markers refer to the entire user task, never one step. For required output, neither supplies synthetic final prose. After ordinary completion validation, missing prose enters final_response_pending and emits completion.direct_deferred, preserving receipts without counting a failed completion negotiation. The next decision retains ordinary authorized tools so the model can finish analysis before delivering the answer. Raw tool output alone cannot satisfy a required answer. Explicit silence retains direct completion; exact text/JSON uses the model's final output without an added recap. Literal phrases such as “Result ready.” are not blacklisted when authored by the model.

Normal tool-then-finish_task workflows retain their turn count. Former direct raw-output completions require an additional answer decision. Saved unfinished runs reuse their receipts; already-terminal history and its presentation remain unchanged. No persistence migration or model-specific policy is involved.

Retained-answer and policy flows connect answer preservation, exact completion reevaluation, atomic scoped settings and domain-owned run recovery.

Evidence, policy and state ownership

completion.py separates declaration corrections from missing evidence and unfinished work. CompletionError preserves its machine reason and exact unmet requirements; CompletionBlocked identifies remaining prerequisites. A declaration-only correction can reuse observed work, while an evidence rejection requires its actual defect to be resolved.

Receipt verification compares the run's result index with the stored receipt. A model-created success entry cannot make a failed, running or unexecuted receipt successful. Job evidence resolves through durable ownership and the matching terminal receipt, including authorized inherited links. A launch acknowledgement alone is insufficient. Capability-specific verify_completion hooks can impose additional deterministic requirements.

The completion bundle is limited to 32 logical evidence groups. An authorized Shell sequence counts as a group only after its manifest and every child have been verified; parent/child overlap does not spend the allowance twice. An unfinished suffix cannot be hidden behind a successful prefix. Automatic selection prioritizes required checks and complete groups, then eligible current-run results. Selection proposes evidence; it does not decide that the user's task is semantically complete.

Caller requirements and optional declaration checks compare actual stored JSON Pointer values. Comparison uses JSON serialization, so JSON true and 1 differ. A current-state requirement considers the newest applicable observation and cannot choose an older matching value after a newer contradiction. Historical execution facts have a separate role; later work does not erase an earlier operation. Self-authored or input-reflected text alone cannot prove an external result, and a silent read command's exit code alone does not prove a requested mutation.

Outcome reporting handles a narrow distinction: a diagnostic command can fail while its observed outcome still answers an accepted request to report what happened. outcome_evidence binds that receipt to an explicit, uniquely identified report_settled_outcome obligation, requires answered status and a required final report, and verifies settled Shell/Python process facts or complete sequences. It never turns a failed diagnostic into evidence of a successful change. Accepted contracts containing requested effects or success-required live observations cannot use that reporting shortcut.

The Agent Checks policy controls receipt verification, model citation, observation completeness, mutation reconciliation and output-status checks at their existing owners. With receipt verification disabled, a validation result can carry receipt_verification="disabled" and zero verified checks; it is not a record that receipts passed verification. Passive monitoring can record a failed check without enforcing it. Required human interaction, terminal continuation routing and accepted deferred waits retain their unconditional boundaries. Other activity, memory and research owners retain their own policies.

Validation is not a pure read. Before testing remaining obligations it calls execution-truth repair, which can settle/save a known operation from definitive same-run receipts without a Gateway or model request. It also updates open_requirements and can record Agent Check observations. completion_preflight can therefore change diagnostic or reconciled state even though it neither publishes terminal acceptance nor executes new work. Callers still own the progression lease and acceptance/publication order.

Completion reporting captures whether original user input requires a final response. Only narrow, standalone silence directives opt out; quoted examples and model choices cannot waive delivery. Missing/older policy versions preserve the existing captured output contract.

Because that policy decides the output contract, the model is not asked to declare it: tool schemas carry no __smto_terminal_output field and the runtime facts omit the declaration guidance. The contract still freezes at the first operational decision, as before. Clarification, discovery and planning controls leave it open, and a text-only first reply is still sent back for a proper decision. Only runs without a policy (resumed historical snapshots) are offered the field. Direct completion uses its accumulated-evidence declaration from the first decision on, and finish_task describes the effective contract. Together these keep the tool list (the start of every request) byte-identical from the first decision, so the inference server can reuse its cached prompt at decision two instead of re-reading the whole request. The module derives counts and safe facts for publication owners without copying tool bodies or creating a model-written fallback.

Publication-contention recovery is separate from semantic completion. If a job was already accepted and Controller publication contends, it retains that operation ID, projects pending recovery facts and wakes the existing watchdog. It tolerates another metadata-write contention because the committed job intent remains. It does not launch a replacement command or treat an unaccepted launch intent as proof of execution.

Terminal normalization considers nonempty prose only for an eligible running conversation. Receipt or control failures propagate; a presentation-contract mismatch keeps verified evidence available for explicit correction. Successful normalization preserves the exact model-authored response rather than synthesizing a replacement answer.

Terminal-control tests, sequence/outcome tests, normalization tests and reporting tests exercise these boundaries with stored fixture receipts and scripted decisions. None of those checks establishes semantic correctness for an arbitrary future user task.

Final-response and argument normalization

terminal_normalization.py handles guarded text-only final responses. It checks pending work, approvals/jobs/task-board state and unresolved mutations through ordinary completion authority. It is unrelated to the target-host terminal process manager. Explicit declarations and response-pending recovery retain their established paths.

schema_correction.py performs transactional argument normalization. Its shared container decoder uses the tool's current argument schema: a string at a field explicitly typed as an object or array can be decoded once as JSON. This works for new tools without adding tool-specific rules, including nested properties, array items, tuple items, typed maps, nullable container types, and local JSON Pointer references. Declared string fields and untyped data remain unchanged. Ambiguous/composed schemas, pattern-based properties, remote references, and reference siblings that add constraints are left to validation. Schema traversal is bounded to 64 levels; it never retrieves external schemas.

Decoding requires complete JSON with unique object keys and finite numbers. It never repairs quotes, brackets, command text, or recursively unwraps a string at the same field. Registered tool/path corrections (such as shared Shell sequence cwd and timeout rules) run after decoding. A candidate is accepted only after the entire result passes strict validation against the supplied schema; any unresolved failure retains the original call. The raw model journal stays unchanged, while corrections are recorded as value-free paths under schema.decode_json_container and executable receipts use the normalized arguments.

Shell command arguments and Shell sequence steps also omit sudo_password and sudo_username when their value is JSON null and the current schema declares them as optional strings. These exact-path rules treat null as no credential supplied; they preserve supplied strings (including empty strings), leave other invalid values to validation, and never traverse opaque input data. Shell parallel and scheduled command children use the same command rules. Required or nullable credential schemas retain their original values. Corrections remain transactional and value-free.

The registered shell.command.close_trailing_literal_quote, shell.sequence.close_trailing_literal_quote, and shell.parallel.close_trailing_literal_quote rules append one missing single or double quote on a final literal operand. They apply to every executable, including write commands and scheduled Shell children. A bounded, non-executing parser proves simple commands, connectors and redirections; balanced commands remain exact. Multiline scripts, substitutions, heredocs, compound grammar, incomplete operators, and tails containing possible omitted shell structure remain unchanged. The fixer never reconstructs a missing operation or replays a failed command. Strict schema validation must accept the entire candidate, and permissions, effect classification, scheduling, receipts and recovery all use the corrected command. The raw model journal remains unchanged and tool.arguments_normalized records only rule/path metadata, never command text.

Shell preflight separately validates heredoc quoting before authorization or command dispatch. An unquoted delimiter such as <<EOF or <<-EOF returns a tool_argument_validation rejection with reason unquoted_heredoc; it does not execute or rewrite any command source. Use <<'EOF', another shell-quoted delimiter, file.write, or stdin_mode=literal with stdin_text for literal content. Deliberate expansion can be expressed in explicit arguments, for example with printf. This applies to ordinary commands and to sequence, parallel and scheduled children through the shared execution preflight, including when strict schema checks are off. Sequences preflight every child before running their first step.

The heredoc check skips quoted words, comments, here-strings, arithmetic expressions and quoted heredoc bodies, and inspects command substitutions. It is a lexical check of supplied Shell source, not a general interpreter or a security sandbox: external scripts, arithmetic contents and program text passed as arguments to other interpreters remain opaque. Locale-dependent delimiters and ANSI-quoted delimiters requiring escape decoding also leave the remaining source opaque. Rejection facts contain the argument path and line, never the heredoc body. Existing missing-quote normalization remains separate.

core/schema_containers.py supplies the schema traversal shared with structural validation. The catalog still checks unambiguous container types when schema.strict_validation is disabled, so an undecodable steps string is rejected before Activity effect inspection. Other strict constraints remain governed by that setting. Normalized arguments still undergo ordinary validation and authorization. Neither normalization system grants new execution authority or rewrites an external result to make it successful.
